raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Naoussa defines Greek red wine aging, and Ramnista sits at the center of that reputation. This single-vineyard selection proves Xinomavro handles oak without losing its savory edge.",
  "wine_summary": "Kir Yianni shifted focus from bulk production to site-specific bottlings within the Naoussa appellation. Ramnista comes from a specific plot where older vines yield lower concentrations of fruit. Consistent medal performance at TEXSOM established a quality benchmark for Xinomavro.",
  "terroir_expression": "Altitudes reaching 300 meters on the slopes of Mount Vermio define the growing site. Sandy loam soils over limestone force roots deep, stressing the vine and thickening skins. That skin contact drives the high tannin count, while the continental climate preserves acidity through hot summers.",
  "vinification_summary": "French and American oak barrels receive the wine after stainless steel fermentation for 18 months. The use of malolactic fermentation softens the sharp malic acid naturally present in Xinomavro, rounding the mid-palate. Basket pressing extracts juice without crushing seeds, limiting bitter phenolics.",
  "food_pairing": "Lamb kleftiko works well because the wine's acidity cuts through the rendered fat. Mushroom risotto matches the earthy notes found in the wine's forest floor aroma. Aged Kasseri cheese provides salt to balance the tannins. Braised beef short ribs offer protein that softens the wine's grip. Grilled octopus with olive oil complements the savory olive notes in the glass.",
  "comparable_wines": "Thymiopoulos Vineyards Young Vines — lighter entry point into the same region. G.D. Vajra Langhe Nebbiolo — similar acid and tannin ratio at a comparable price. Domaine Faiveley Mercurey — offers the earthy red fruit profile without the Greek indigenous variety.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and savory earth notes",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Decant for one hour if drinking young vintages to soften tannins. Store horizontally at 55°F to keep the cork moist and prevent oxidation.",
  "value_assessment": "$29.46 places this above entry-level Greek reds but below premium Barolo. You pay for the single-vineyard designation compared to Thymiopoulos Ouranos at $20. The cost is justified by the aging potential that cheaper regional blends lack.",
  "market_position": "On restaurant lists, this wine offers Old World structure without French pricing. Collectors buy multiple vintages to track how Xinomavro evolves over decades. Casual drinkers often find the tannins too aggressive until the wine opens up.",
  "insider_take": "Buyers seeking a smooth Tuesday night pour should look at Agiorgitiko instead. The tradeoff for that austerity is a complexity that softens only after five years in bottle. Skip this bottle if you want immediate fruit sweetness.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,
  "sensory": {
